scenarios.title: Operating Carrier · Hub-and-Spoke · Cross-Dock
scenarios.summary: Activates carrier responsibility, terminal specialization, consolidation and intermediate cross-dock emphasis.

scenarios.title: Shipper · Direct Shipment
scenarios.summary: Permitted variant only when contracted service supports bypass of terminal consolidation/deconsolidation; the composer marks bypassed network records without deleting them from the LTL universe.

scenarios.title: 3PL · Hub-and-Spoke · Finance lens
scenarios.summary: Keeps one operating graph while shifting responsibility metadata and focusing preliminary charge, audit and settlement controls.

scenarios.title: United States · Dangerous Goods
scenarios.summary: Loads North-American LTL/classification context plus U.S. hazardous-material evidence because country scope is explicitly United States; commodity and provision-level applicability still require resolution.

scenarios.title: CMR scope · Dangerous Goods
scenarios.summary: CMR and dangerous-goods scope are resolved independently; ADR is not inferred merely from CMR.

scenarios.title: India · Dangerous Goods
scenarios.summary: E-way-bill evidence is available, but the complete current national/state dangerous-goods source pack is not frozen.

scenarios.title: Temperature Controlled
scenarios.summary: Activates equipment/condition controls. ATP remains a candidate source and is not activated until specified goods and legal scope resolve.

scenarios.title: Customs Transit
scenarios.summary: Activates regulatory status, hold/release and evidence. TIR remains a candidate source and is not inferred from customs-transit selection alone.

scenarios.title: Bonded context
scenarios.summary: Activates inventory/custody segregation and authority hold/release; national authorization remains required.

scenarios.title: Multimodal / Intermodal relationship
scenarios.summary: Activates leg-by-leg interchange. Each non-road leg retains its carrier, document, regime and jurisdiction.
